<action type="say">
Here’s how to do this directly on JetBlue’s website and how to see refund vs credit.

STEP 1 – Go to your trip on jetblue.com  
1) Open a browser and go to: https://www.jetblue.com  
2) At the top, click “Manage Trips” (sometimes “Manage trips / Check in”).  
3) Under “Find your trip” (or similar), choose the option to look up by confirmation code.  
4) Enter:
   - Confirmation code: BK-B65510-20261101  
   - Last name: Petrovic  
5) Click “Continue” or “Find flight” to open your November 1 itinerary.

STEP 2 – Start the cancellation flow  
6) On the trip details page, look for a button or link such as:
   - “Cancel flight”  
   - “Cancel this trip”  
   - Or under “Change or cancel”  
7) Click that. This will take you to a page that shows what you’ll get back if you cancel.

STEP 3 – See if it’s a refund or Travel Bank credit  
On the cancellation/confirmation screen (before you finalize), carefully read the summary box. You’ll typically see something like:

- If it’s a REFUND to your card/original payment, look for wording like:
  - “Refund to original form of payment: $XXX.XX”  
  - “Amount to be refunded: $XXX.XX”  
  - “Refund method: Original form of payment”  
  - Or a line item clearly saying “Refund” with your card type (e.g., VISA ****1234).

- If it’s a JETBLUE TRAVEL BANK CREDIT, look for wording like:
  - “Credit to JetBlue Travel Bank: $XXX.XX”  
  - “This nonrefundable fare will be issued as a JetBlue Travel Bank credit.”  
  - “Funds will be deposited into your Travel Bank account.”  
  - A line that mentions “Travel Bank” instead of “refund.”

There may also be a short fare note on that page:
- “Refundable” → usually means money can go back to your original form of payment if no fees apply.  
- “Nonrefundable” → usually means you’ll receive a Travel Bank credit (minus any fees), not cash back.

Before you click the final “Confirm” or “Cancel flight” button, make sure the summary clearly matches what you want (refund vs credit and the dollar amount).

STEP 4 – Complete the cancellation  
8) Once you confirm what you’re getting back, click the final button (e.g., “Confirm cancellation,” “Yes, cancel,” etc.).  
9) Wait for the confirmation screen. It should show:
   - That the flight/trip is cancelled  
   - The amount refunded or credited  
   - Where it’s going (Travel Bank vs original payment)  

STEP 5 – Verify after cancellation  
10) Check your email (nikola.petrovic@bg.ac.rs) for a cancellation confirmation from JetBlue. It usually states:
    - Whether you received a refund or Travel Bank credit  
    - The exact amount  
11) If it’s a refund:
    - The email will say something like “refund to original form of payment.”  
    - The money may take a few business days to appear on your card statement.  
12) If it’s a Travel Bank credit:
    - The email will mention Travel Bank and the credited amount.  
    - You can log into your JetBlue account → look for “Travel Bank” or “Credits” to see the balance.

If you’d like, you can describe exactly what you see on the cancellation screen (the text around the amount you’re getting back), and I can help you interpret whether it’s a refund or a credit before you click the final confirm button.</action>
